# SeaweedFS original source bytes

These24 public files come from Git blobs in SeaweedFS commit `c5073360007d28385a33426a42ac3e4ec504c5a3`, tree `bce9e3f66721208f35888124183f80bd76d64f90`: two module files, five packaging/licence materials and17 original Go files changed by the copy-lock repair. They are unmodified LF bytes, captured through binary Git output and written directly as buffers. Git attributes disable checkout conversion for the `upstream` directory. The upstream root and glog licenses are included.

The source diagnostic validates these files before applying its separately locked complete patch. The regression test checks every original identity, rejects CRLF conversions, applies the module/Go patch to all original files, verifies the exact changed-path set and checks every resulting identity. It does not download or execute SeaweedFS, the copied upstream workflows or their dependencies. The full native source diagnostic remains a separate requirement.

The pristine credential test contains two copies of AWS's [published documentation credential example](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdkref/latest/guide/feature-static-credentials.html). The supplemental high-confidence detector exempts only that exact example/count in this exact path and immutable9,321-byte fixture, SHA-256 `4dbc7dcaa2f1e391499a141222dc9ebbb1ff52c6dc20ef1f2b3c0e560a3e3251`. Secretlint still scans the unchanged original file. Any byte/path change, extra occurrence or another credential invalidates the exception; there is no global sample ignore or source-fixture exclusion.
